dataset_metadata.description: A legal domain dataset consisting of 1,104 U.S. Supreme Court verdicts. It pairs full-text official court documents with thematic categories and synthetic summaries generated by the Command R+ (cmd-r+) language model.

schema_analysis.description: The legal taxonomy or subject matter classification of the case (e.g., 'Voting & Elections', 'Trademarks').
The official title or formal name of the Supreme Court case.
The source URL pointing to the full case record on Justia.
The full-length official text of the Supreme Court opinion and syllabus.
An AI-generated summary of the case's facts, legal questions, and the Court's ruling.

structural_logic.relationships: The 'document' serves as the ground-truth source material; 'summary' is a synthetic transformation of 'document'; 'category' acts as a categorical label for the document-summary pair.
structural_logic.label_dynamics: The dataset includes 27 unique legal categories, facilitating multi-class classification tasks alongside summarization.
structural_logic.potential_bottlenecks: Extreme variance in document length (ranging from ~1,500 to ~700,000 characters) creates significant challenges for standard context windows; synthetic summaries may inherit biases or hallucinations from the generating model.
